text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert — SEV2: repeated runtime OOMs observed in us-east-1-dedicated-2 pool. 33 OOM errors in 10m, spike at 2026-03-15T10:31:51Z. Paging: @ryan_oncall.

ryan_oncall: Acked. I'm on it. First priority: contain customer impact and stop further OOMs. Who can run quick mitigations (drop batching / lower concurrency)?

maria_runtime: I can do immediate changes. Suggest: 1) turn off autoscale-batching 2) reduce concurrent sessions on that pool to 32 3) trim large in-memory caches. Doing now.

maria_runtime: Running:
```sh
# reduce concurrency
redwoodctl pool update us-east-1-dedicated-2 --concurrency=32
# disable autosized batching
redwoodctl runtime config set --pool us-east-1-dedicated-2 batching.enabled=false
# trim prefix cache to 50%
runtimetool cache trim --pool us-east-1-dedicated-2 --percent=50
```

logs-bot: Upload complete: https://logs.internal/redwood/2240001111/oom-samples.tgz (access: eng/runtime). Included: gpu_alloc_stats.txt, allocator_profile.json, sample request logs.

maria_runtime: Quick tail from gpu_alloc_stats.txt:
```
[2026-03-15T10:31:50Z] GPU0 total=49152MB used=44123MB free=5029MB largest_free_block=64MB fragmentation_ratio=0.85
[2026-03-15T10:31:50Z] attempted_alloc=256MB -> OOM
[2026-03-15T10:31:51Z] jemalloc: retained=8GB active=41GB mapped=45GB
```

eva_sre: fragmentation_ratio 0.85 is high. Looks like allocator fragmentation (largest free chunk only 64MB) — multiple small frees preventing coalescing. That would cause fail for larger transient allocations even if total free appears OK.

chris_support: Customer impact check: initial query shows ~7 customers got 5xx on chat/generate endpoint between 10:30-10:35. Biggest: AcmeMaps (service_id: svc-acme-01) saw ~5% requests failing. I'm looping in Support for postmortem notices.

ryan_oncall: Good. Maria — did flipping batching off reduce the OOM rate?

maria_runtime: After changes (10:33Z) we see OOM events drop from 33 in 10m -> 3 in next 10m. Trimming cache gave immediate headroom. No full customer outage. Routing still at ~95% normal.

eva_sre: For RCA we need: full allocator profile, jemalloc stats, GPU cgroups + nvidia-smi pmon around the spike, and the request size distribution for that minute. I started a small timeline doc: https://notebook.internal/redwood/incidents/2240001111/timeline (eng/runtime access).

maria_runtime: Pushing allocator profile and raw allocator logs to the notebook. Also saved the sample request that triggered the large alloc.

ryan_oncall: Hypotheses (initial):
1) Long-lived prefix/KV cache created memory fragmentation (many small frees + retained slabs) causing large allocs to fail.
2) Autoscaled batching created a transient burst (single request expanded into a very large batch due to timing) that required a contiguous block larger than any free chunk.
3) jemalloc arena exhaustion / fragmentation bug in our allocation patterns (edge case with large embeddings + kv-reserved buffers).

maria_runtime: Supporting data: the allocator profile shows many old extents retained; free lists dominated by small chunks. Also see frequent small evictions (4-16KB) in KV cache logs around 10:29-10:31Z.

logs-bot: Sample request headers for the big request:
```json
{"user":"svc-acme-01","seq_len":4096,"prompt_prefix_kv":true,"batching_hint":true}
```

eva_sre: That matches hypothesis #2 + #1. Long prefix cache + one request with seq_len 4096 can force KV materialization and create several large contiguous allocations. If allocator can't coalesce, OOM.

chris_support: Customer communication plan: send T+2 initial summary to affected customers, note mitigation steps and ETA for RCA (target 72h). AcmeMaps ops contact already notified.

ryan_oncall: Action items (owners):
- Full jemalloc heap dump & analysis -> @maria_runtime (in 2h)
- Reproduce locally with synthetic workload (big prefixes + variable batch) -> @maria_runtime + @maria_runtime (test harness)
- Short-term change: keep batching disabled for us-east-1-dedicated-2 and reduce cache default retention by 30% -> @maria_runtime (done)
- Longer-term: add allocator defrag path + detect fragmentation threshold to auto-evict -> @eva_sre + eng/runtime (RFC)
- Customer comms -> @chris_support

maria_runtime: I'll attach jemalloc stats here once processed. Preliminary: arenas=8, dirty pages reclaimed gradually but fragmentation persistent.

deploy-bot: Canary task queued: disable prefix-cache for 5% of traffic on us-east-1-dedicated-2 for 30m -> task id canary-2240001111-1.

eva_sre: For the in-thread timeline, I'm adding these events:
- 10:30:12Z spike in small eviction rate
- 10:31:51Z OOM cluster spike (33 errors/10m window)
- 10:33:00Z batching disabled + cache trim -> OOM rate drops to baseline
- 10:40:00Z canary toggle started

ryan_oncall: Please keep posting logs/snippets in this thread. We'll treat this as the canonical coordination thread for RCA until we open the formal postmortem.

maria_runtime: Attached a small jemalloc snippet:
```
# jemalloc stats summary (post-trim)
active: 41.2GB
metadata: 1.1GB
retained: 7.9GB
largest_free: 64MB
small_bin_frees: 120k (increase around 10:29)
```

chris_support: Noted. I'll draft the customer note and send the T+2 in the morning.

eva_sre: Hypothesis prioritization: 1 and 2 are highest. Repro attempt should try: heavy prefix cache + a single large incoming sequence + batching enabled to trigger the contiguous alloc. If we can repro, mitigation options: allocator defrag, enforce max contiguous alloc size (reject or stream), or pre-commit contiguous buffers.

ryan_oncall: Closing loop for now: oncall stays watching. If OOMs reappear >5/minute we re-open paging. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
